tools.name: Pacer
tools.subtitle: min per mark
tools.help:
Pacer
Times a practice paper against a plan.

1. Enter minutes, marks and the
   checkpoint size.
2. EXE starts the clock.
3. F1 logs a mark, F2 pauses.

The gap line says how far ahead or
behind the plan you are.

Keys: EXE start/stop, F1 mark, F2
pause, F3 finish, EXIT back.
tools.summary: Minutes per mark, checkpoint times, and a live gap line: “Behind by 1m20s”.
tools.body: Enter the length of the paper and how many marks it carries. Bench splits it into checkpoints and then runs the clock against them, four redraws a second so the battery is not asked for more.
points: Setup: total minutes, total marks, marks per checkpoint.
90 minutes and 80 marks gives 1.125 min/mark and eight checkpoints.
Run: F1 logs a mark, F2 pauses, F3 finishes. The gap line is the point.
Done: total time and the final gap, nothing to write down.
tools.leadCaption: Finished: total time and final gap
shots: The plan: min/mark and every checkpoint time
Running: clock, marks logged, gap line
Finished: total time and final gap

tools.name: Cards
tools.subtitle: flashcards
tools.help:
Cards
Flashcards with a Leitner schedule.

A deck is one file in Bench/cards,
one card per line:
   question | answer

Right answers move a card to the
next box, wrong ones send it back.
Progress is saved when the session
ends, never during it.

Keys: EXE reveal/mark, F1 right,
F2 wrong, EXIT back.
tools.summary: A flashcard drill over a plain text deck, spaced across three boxes.
tools.body: Decks are text you can write anywhere: one card a line, question and answer split by a vertical bar. Right moves a card up a box, wrong sends it back to box 1, and boxes 2 and 3 come round less often.
points: “What is the unit of impulse? | N s” is a whole card.
500 cards a deck, 120 characters a side; a broken line is reported with its number.
Progress is keyed by a hash of the question, so editing an answer keeps its box.
Saved once, when the session ends, never inside the loop.
tools.leadCaption: The answer, and F1 / F2 to grade it
shots: A deck: cards per box and when it is due
The answer, and F1 / F2 to grade it

tools.name: Notes
tools.subtitle: Markdown
tools.help:
Notes
Reads .md and .txt from Bench/notes.

Markdown headings, lists, quotes,
bold and code are drawn in the
palette. Long lines wrap; the wrap
width is a setting.

Keys: UP/DOWN scroll, EXE page down,
ALPHA search, F2 headings, EXIT.
tools.summary: Read text and a Markdown subset from the calculator's storage, with search.
tools.body: Drop .md and .txt files into Bench/notes and read them on the calculator. Headings, bold, italic, code, lists, quotes and checkboxes are styled with colour and rules rather than extra fonts, so nothing has to be installed.
points: Up to 32 KiB a file, long lines wrapped to the screen or to a set width.
F1 search, F2 next hit, F3 the heading list, F4 back to the top.
Characters the calculator font lacks are drawn as ? and counted in the footer.
tools/md2bench.py maps typographic symbols down to ASCII before you copy.
tools.leadCaption: A Markdown note: headings, bold, a list
shots: A Markdown note: headings, bold, a list
Jump to any heading with F3
Scrolling a long note by page

tools.name: Function
tools.subtitle: x and f(x)
tools.help:
Function table
A table and a value for f(x).

1. Pick a slot f, g, h, p, q, r.
2. EXE types the expression on the
   keyboard: x, pi, e, + - * / ^,
   sin cos tan ln log sqrt abs.
3. F1 opens the table.

In the table: LEFT/RIGHT move the
start, F1 changes the step, F2 the
row count, EXE probes one value.
F4 switches degrees and radians;
the mode shows in the title bar.

Slots are written to
Bench/state/exprs.txt when you
leave the tool.

Keys: EXE edit, F1 table, F3 clear.
tools.summary: One engine for x, pi, e and twenty functions, behind a table and a probe.
tools.body: Type an expression once on the on-screen keyboard and keep it in one of six slots: f, g, h, p, q, r. A shunting-yard parser holds its operator stack in a fixed 32 entries, so a long expression cannot overflow the calculator's stack, and an error names the column it failed at.
points: Implicit multiplication: 3x, 2(x+1), (x+1)(x-1), 2pi.
A table of x and f(x) from a start value, a step and a count; F2 probes one value.
Six expressions live in RAM and reach Bench/state/exprs.txt when you leave the tool.
tools.leadCaption: Six expressions, and a table of one of them
shots: The six slots and their expressions
A table of x against f(x)

tools.name: Triangle
tools.subtitle: sides, angles
tools.help:
Triangle
Three sides and three angles. Fill
in what you know and leave the rest
blank.

Give any three values, at least one
a side: SSS, SAS, ASA and AAS all
solve, and the fields fill in.

SSA - two sides and an angle not
between them - can have two answers.
The title bar then says so and F2
swaps between the two triangles.

Area and perimeter are under the
fields.  F3 degrees, F4 radians.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
EXE solves, F1 clears.
tools.summary: Any three of the six values in, every side, angle, the area and the perimeter out.
tools.body: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and SSA go through the law of cosines and the law of sines. The SSA case says when there are two triangles instead of quietly picking one, and the six boxes sit in the shape of the triangle: a b c over A B C, each angle under the side it is opposite.
points: 3, 4, 5 gives C = 90°, A = 36.87°, area 6 and perimeter 12.
SSA with a = 10, b = 15, A = 30° reports two triangles; F2 swaps between them.
Worked lines for the cosine rule and the sine rule.
F3 degrees, F4 radians, and the unit is in the title bar.
tools.leadCaption: 3, 4, 5: the right angle, the area, the perimeter
shots: 3, 4, 5: the right angle, the area, the perimeter
The SSA case, with both triangles available

tools.name: Polynomials
tools.subtitle: roots, expand
tools.help:
Polynomials
Quadratics, expansion and rational
roots.

Three screens, F4 or F2 next and F3
back:
  Quadratic  a, b, c give the
             discriminant, both roots
             and the vertex.
  Expand     (ax + b)^n to degree 8.
  Roots      c0..cn as coefficients;
             whole and half roots are
             found, the rest is shown.

Arrows move between fields, digits
type, DEL deletes, F1 clears.  F2 on
the roots screen adds a coefficient.

Rounding is half up on the digits.
tools.summary: Quadratics, expansion and division, with the discriminant, the vertex and the factors.
tools.body: Three screens over one fixed-size polynomial type: a quadratic that shows the discriminant, both roots, the vertex and the factor pair; an expansion of (ax + b)^n term by term; and a coefficient list whose rational roots are hunted by the rational root theorem.
points: x² - 5x + 6: discriminant 1, roots 3 and 2, vertex (2.5, -0.25).
x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 factors as (x - 3)(x - 2)(x - 1).
Divide x³ - 2x² - 4 by x - 3: quotient x² + x + 3, remainder 5.
Coefficients are typed rather than parsed, because the keypad has no letters for x².
tools.leadCaption: A quadratic: discriminant, roots, vertex, factor pair
shots: A quadratic: discriminant, roots, vertex, factor pair

tools.name: Root finder
tools.subtitle: bisect, Newton
tools.help:
Root finder
Solves f(x) = 0 one step at a time,
so the convergence is visible.

F2 picks the method:
  bisection needs a and b with a
    sign change between them
  Newton needs one guess x0
  secant needs two guesses x0, x1

F3 solves. The table lists n, x and
f(x); the plot marks every iterate.

Radians always, whatever the angle
setting says. Tolerance 1e-6, at most
50 steps.

Keys: EXE edits f or solves, F1 clears,
F2 method, arrows move and scroll.
tools.summary: f(x) = 0 one step at a time, with every iterate in a table and marked on the curve.
tools.body: Bisection, Newton and the secant method over an expression from the expression engine. Newton takes its slope from a central difference with a step of 1e-6, so no derivative has to be typed, and the table of n, x, f(x) and the step size shows the error falling rather than asserting that it does.
points: Newton on x² - 2 from 1: 1.5, 1.416667, 1.414216, root 1.414214 in four steps.
Bisection on [1, 2] reaches the same root in twenty.
No sign change and a zero slope are refused with a sentence, not guessed at.
Radians always, said in the title bar, with a 50-step cap.
tools.leadCaption: Newton: four iterates and the plot that marks them
shots: Newton: four iterates and the plot that marks them
A bracket with no sign change

tools.name: Sequences
tools.subtitle: terms, sums
tools.help:
Sequences
Arithmetic and geometric terms,
their sums, and binomials.

Three screens, F4 next and F3 back.

  Arithmetic  a, d, n: the nth term
              and the sum, then the
              first few terms.
  Geometric   a, r, n: as above, plus
              the sum to infinity when
              |r| < 1.
  Binomial    n choose k exactly, and
              row n of Pascal.

Terms count from 1, so the first term
is n = 1.  C(n,k) is refused rather
than rounded when it passes 64 bits.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
EXE solves, F1 clears.
tools.summary: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, the sum to infinity, and binomial coefficients.
tools.body: Terms and partial sums for both kinds of sequence, with the first few terms listed under the answer so the pattern is visible. The binomial screen works through Pascal's row, one term of (ax + b)^n, and a coefficient at a chosen power.
points: u₁ = 3, d = 4: u₁₀ = 39 and S₁₀ = 210.
u₁ = 2, r = 3: u₅ = 162 and S₅ = 242; with r = 0.5 the sum to infinity of 8 is 16.
C(n,k) cancels before it multiplies, so C(62,31) still fits in 64 bits.
A coefficient that would pass 64 bits is refused rather than printed wrong.
tools.leadCaption: Arithmetic: u₁₀ and S₁₀, with the terms underneath
shots: Arithmetic: u₁₀ and S₁₀, with the terms underneath
Pascal's row and a binomial coefficient

tools.name: Complex
tools.subtitle: a + bi
tools.help:
Complex numbers
Two numbers a and b, one operation
at a time.

F2 picks the operation: a + b,
a - b, a x b, a / b and a ^ n, where
n is the real part of b.

The result is written three ways:
rectangular (-1 + 2i), its modulus
and argument, and polar form.

F3 shows the argument in degrees,
F4 in radians.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
DEL deletes, F1 clears, EXIT home.
tools.summary: Rectangular, modulus-and-argument and polar form on one screen.
tools.body: Two numbers, one operation at a time, and the answer written three ways so it is obvious they are the same number. Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and integer powers, with the argument taken in the angle mode you picked.
points: 1 + i has modulus 1.414214 and argument 45°; (1 + i)⁴ = -4.
Dividing by 0 + 0i says “not a number” instead of printing an infinity.
F2 cycles the operation, F3 and F4 pick degrees or radians.
tools.leadCaption: A product in all three forms
shots: A product in all three forms

tools.name: Number theory
tools.subtitle: gcd to CRT
tools.help:
Number theory
Nine functions, each with working.

gcd, lcm, prime test, factorise,
modular inverse, CRT, divisors,
totient and base conversion.

Factorisation shows a progress bar;
EXIT cancels it.

Keys: UP/DOWN choose, EXE open,
EXIT back.
tools.summary: gcd to CRT, in 64-bit integer arithmetic: no floats, no rounding surprises.
tools.body: Nine functions behind one menu, with the working shown where the working is the point, such as Euclid's steps for gcd or an extended gcd. Inputs up to 18 digits are exact.
points: gcd, lcm, extended gcd with Bézout coefficients, modular inverse.
modpow by square and multiply with mulmod, so 2^64 mod 1000 is exact.
Deterministic Miller-Rabin primality test for the whole 64-bit range.
Factor by trial division then Pollard rho, with a progress bar and EXIT to cancel.
Euler's totient and the Chinese remainder theorem, one pair or a whole list.

tools.name: Uncertainty
tools.subtitle: value and error
tools.help:
Uncertainty
Arithmetic with errors, to 1 or 2
significant figures.

Type a value and its absolute error,
pick an operation, type the second
value and error.

Chain mode keeps the result as the
first value of the next step.

Keys: F1..F3 operation, EXE apply,
EXIT back.
tools.summary: Add, subtract, multiply, divide and raise measured values, errors included.
tools.body: Two values with their errors, one operation, and a result in the shape a physics teacher wants: value, absolute uncertainty, percentage. F1 feeds the result back in as A and you keep going.
points: A + B and A - B add the absolute errors; A * B and A / B add the relative ones.
A ^ n and k * A are covered too, with the exact rule for each.
Rounding is half-up on decimal digits, never on the binary float: 0.15 goes to 0.2.
One figure for the uncertainty, or two when its first digit is 1.
shots: Choosing the operation and the second operand

tools.name: Sig figs
tools.subtitle: round, standard
tools.help:
Sig figs
How many figures, and how to write
them.

UP/DOWN picks a mode, LEFT/RIGHT
changes n, EXE types the number.

Count: leading zeros never count,
and trailing zeros count only after
a decimal point. 0.004560 has 4.

Round: half up on the decimal
digits, so 1234.5 to 3 figures is
1230 = 1.23 x 10^3.

Practice asks a question; type the
count and EXE marks it, F2 moves
on.

Keys: EXE type, F1 clear.
tools.summary: Significant figures counted on the text rather than the value, plus standard form and SI prefixes.
tools.body: Six modes: count the figures, round to a number of figures, round to a number of decimals, standard form, SI prefix, and a practice mode that asks and marks. Figures are counted on the characters you typed, which is why 1200 has two and 1200. has four.
points: 0.004560 has 4 figures and is 4.560 × 10⁻³.
1234.5 to 3 figures is 1230, written 1.23 × 10³.
4560 with a prefix is 4.56 k; 1e-9 is 1.00 n.
Rounding is half-up on the decimal digits, never on the binary float.
tools.leadCaption: Count the figures, then round a third
shots: Counting the figures in a typed number
Count the figures, then round a third
